text:
andrea: scan caught a high-risk OpenSSL CVE in `gcr.io/redwood/base:2026-04-02` (CVE-2026-7777). It shows up in a distro layer. should we trigger rebuild + signing?

samir: paste the scanner lines + layer sha pls

andrea: snippet:
```
CVE-2026-7777 | openssl 3.1.0 | RCE | CVSS 9.6
file: /usr/lib/libssl.so.3
layer: sha256:beefc0de...1234
```

maria: even if upstream, we should rebuild to control the final artifact (strip tooling, lock perms). also we should extend audit retention for signing and KMS calls for the incident window. compliance will want it.

leo: KMS question: our signer key resource is `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/image/cryptoKeys/signer-v3`. if we create a new keyversion to sign the patched image, can we still verify old signatures after switching primary?

security-oncall: yes — signatures embed the key version used. verification uses the public material of that version. do NOT disable old versions until all images signed by them are retired. recommended: keep old versions enabled for at least 14 days; 30 days preferred for safety.

ci-bot: vuln-alert -> gcr.io/redwood/base:2026-04-02 -> CVE-2026-7777 (9.6) -> ticket INC-812 created.

andrea: proposed short plan:
- pause new canaries and batch pushes
- create patched base in staging: apply distro fixes, remove package manager + debug symbols, set file permissions to 0644/0755 as appropriate
- build + smoke tests (startup, attestation, perf p95)
- cosign sign + attest with current signer keyversion (no rotation yet)
- 2% canary for 30m, watch for cosign verify errors, startup crashes, telemetry regressions
- ramp if green; schedule key rotation only after cleanup window

samir: volunteering for canary watch. opening IAM MR to grant CI-SA scoped signer permission to staging key only. MR: https://gitlab.com/redwood/infra/merge_requests/345 (binding snippet in MR).

maria: I'll open SIEM retention PR to extend image-sign and KMS audit logs from 30d -> 180d for org `redwood-prod`. filing ticket SIEM-1256 and linking to INC-812.

infra-oncall: FYI — if the CI pipeline needs direct KMS encrypt/decrypt, prefer short-lived SA keys and limited IAM binding rather than broad project roles. also watch rate limits on KMS for high churn.

leo: follow-up: what's the revoke cadence? we should document a safe-flow in the incident note.

security-oncall: policy draft for this incident: do not disable key versions for 14 days after last prod image signed by them; target 30 days. post intent 48h in #release-war-room prior to disable. after revoke, ensure COSIGN verification against archived public keys for forensic needs.

andrea: kicking off staging build now. will post build id + cosign logs.

ci-bot: build started: staging/base:2026-04-02-patched #5020

maria: SIEM ticket created and linked to the incident. PR for retention change in internal infra repo assigned to infra-oncall. ETA ~2h.

samir: IAM MR opened and requested reviewers from infra and security. adding temporary `keystore.signer` binding scoped to `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/image/cryptoKeys/signer-v3/cryptoKeyVersions/1` for CI-SA only.

security-oncall: assigning owners: andrea(build + validation), samir(canary + IAM), maria(audit retention + compliance). infra-oncall if KMS ops needed. ping me on any cosign/KMS deny.

(andrea later): staging build finished. cosign attest OK. scheduling 2% canary at 13:40 UTC for 30m. samir on watch. :thumbsup:
